questions.q: What is the real purpose of an incident response plan, according to this lesson?
options: A document that is only reviewed once a year and never opened otherwise
A reference document the team actually uses during a live incident, not a binder written only to satisfy an audit
A list of every employee's job title, unrelated to security events
A marketing document meant to reassure customers
questions.explain: A real plan is designed to be opened and followed under pressure, often at 2 a.m., not filed away after approval.

questions.q: Why must severity classification criteria be decided in advance rather than judged case-by-case?
options: Because severity classification has nothing to do with the communication plan
So the team doesn't have to debate how serious an incident is while the clock is already running
Because regulators require every incident to be rated the same severity
Because severity never actually changes how an organization responds
questions.explain: Predefined criteria, like "ransomware with lateral movement = SEV1," let the team act immediately instead of arguing about the rating.

questions.q: What does a communication plan define within an IR plan?
options: Only the names of customers who must never be told about an incident
The programming language used by the SOC's tools
The marketing copy used in a press release after an incident
Exactly who gets notified, in what order, and within what time window, for each severity level
questions.explain: The communication plan spells out notification order and timing so nothing depends on memory during a crisis.

questions.q: Why does a real IR plan need a tool and access inventory that includes offline or out-of-band options?
options: Because the inventory is only used for employee onboarding, not incident response
Because regulators forbid using any cloud-based tools during an incident
Because offline tools are always faster than online ones
Because the normal network, credentials, or communication tools might themselves be down or compromised during the incident
questions.explain: If Active Directory or the usual password manager is part of what's compromised, the team needs another way to reach credentials and each other.

questions.q: What kind of deadline does the legal and regulatory notification section of an IR plan address?
options: The internal deadline for finishing a quarterly budget report
A deadline that only applies to companies with no customer data at all
Real external deadlines such as GDPR's 72-hour window, state breach-notification laws, HIPAA, PCI DSS, or SEC disclosure rules
The expiration date of the company's office lease
questions.explain: These are real legal and contractual obligations that can start a countdown the moment certain types of data are exposed.
